skill.name: kleros-curate
skill.description: Guide Kleros Curate registry work across Light Curate, Stake Curate, and Scout, including submissions, challenges, appeals, deployment, and verification.
skill.summary: Prepare and validate Kleros Curate registry operations using live policies, schemas, deposits, and contract state.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: All 109 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, public URLs, schema terms, and task-specific blockchain validation. No prompt injection or secret collection was found. The skill still enables high-impact onchain actions that can spend funds or transfer control.

remediation.issue: Onchain actions can spend or lock funds and can transfer registry control.
remediation.suggestion: Require final approval showing chain, contract, method, asset, amount, recipient, allowance, and decoded calldata before every transaction.

remediation.issue: ERC20 approvals can expose more funds than the intended registry action requires.
remediation.suggestion: Use exact allowances, verify token and spender addresses, and recommend revoking unused allowances after completion.

remediation.issue: Administrative changes can alter registry policy, economics, timing, or governance.
remediation.suggestion: Require governor identity verification, parameter diffs, simulation results, and explicit confirmation immediately before each administrative call.

content.value_statement: Curate operations require live policy, schema, deposit, and contract checks. This skill guides validated submissions, challenges, appeals, deployments, and registry verification.
actual_capabilities: Distinguishes Light Curate, Stake Curate, and Scout using user context and contract checks.
Retrieves live MetaEvidence to identify policies and exact item schemas.
Builds and validates item metadata from authoritative registry columns.
Calculates live deposits, stakes, arbitration costs, and appeal funding requirements.
Guides submissions, challenges, evidence, withdrawals, deployments, and list verification.
Queries Scout and Stake Curate data through documented endpoints and onchain fallbacks.
limitations: Supports Kleros Curate variants, not unrelated registries or general blockchain administration.
Requires working RPC, IPFS, and sometimes Goldsky access.
Cannot guarantee transaction success, policy acceptance, juror outcomes, or endpoint availability.
Onchain actions can spend or lock funds and require careful user review.

use_cases.title: Launch a Curated Registry
use_cases.description: Prepare policies, MetaEvidence, deposits, deployment parameters, and frontend verification steps for a new registry.

use_cases.title: Submit or Challenge Items
use_cases.description: Validate registry policy, build item data or evidence, calculate live costs, and prepare a transaction.

use_cases.title: Operate Existing Registries
use_cases.description: Inspect status, fund appeals, recover rewards, manage withdrawals, and prepare approved administrative changes.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Registry Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify whether this Kleros registry uses Light Curate, Stake Curate, or Scout. Ask for any missing chain or address details.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Item
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the latest MetaEvidence for [registry], summarize the policy, list required fields, and draft a validated submission without sending a transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge an Entry
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [item] against the active policy, prepare evidence, compute the live challenge deposit, and stop before submission for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy and Verify a Registry
prompt_templates.prompt: Design MetaEvidence and parameters for a new [LGTCR or PGTCR] registry on [chain]. Validate, simulate, and prepare list verification steps.

output_examples.input: Identify the Curate flavor for a Gnosis registry that matches a known Scout address.
output_examples.output: Scout overlay confirmed on Light Curate. Use Scout templates with LightGeneralizedTCR contract operations and xDAI deposit calculations.

output_examples.input: Prepare a token submission after retrieving the active registry policy and schema.
output: Required columns listed in authoritative order.
Submission values validated with no placeholders.
Live deposit calculation and simulation remain required before approval.

output_examples.input: Check whether the challenger can still fund an appeal round.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the current ruling, deadline, paid amount, remaining contribution, and any stop condition before transaction preparation.

best_practices: Fetch current contract state, MetaEvidence, and economic parameters for every operation.
Read the active policy and preserve registry column labels, order, types, and identifiers exactly.
Simulate the exact call and obtain explicit approval before any upload, approval, or transaction.
anti_patterns: Reuse cached deposits, arbitration costs, schemas, addresses, or challenge deadlines.
Guess field names, normalize type strings, or submit placeholder values.
Upload drafts or send transactions before policy review, simulation, and user approval.

faq.question: Which Kleros registries are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Light Curate, Stake Curate, Scout registries, and the documented Classic list verification workflow.

faq.question: Does the skill send blockchain transactions?
faq.answer: It can prepare transaction steps. Execution should occur only after simulation and explicit user approval.

faq.question: What information is required?
faq.answer: Provide the target chain, registry address or URL, requested action, and required item or evidence values.

faq.question: Does it need a Goldsky token?
faq.answer: Public Stake Curate endpoints do not require a token. Private endpoints can use a securely handled bearer token.

faq.question: Why does it use IPFS?
faq.answer: Curate stores policies, evidence, schemas, and item metadata through content-addressed references that must remain available during disputes.

faq.question: Can it guarantee acceptance or rewards?
faq.answer: No. Registry policies, challenges, juror rulings, governance changes, and network conditions determine final outcomes.
